properties.description: Cobalt complex with two phenanthroline ligands and two hydroxide ligands

nodes.name: Co-phen complex formation
nodes.procedure: The Co-phen solutions were prepared by adding 4 mM CoCl2·6H2O, 14 mM phenanthroline into 40 mL deionized H2O, and thereafter mixed with 2.0 M NaOH (v/v = 1:1) to form Co(phen)2(OH)2 containing electrolyte. UV-Vis in combination with EPR suggest a hydroxyl-involved Co-N coordination state. 18O-labeled and D-labeled FT-ICR-MS confirms that the molecular formula is Co(phen)2(OH)2.
nodes.source_text: The Co-phen solutions were prepared by adding 4 mM CoCl2·6H2O, 14 mM phenanthroline into 40 mL deionized H2O... UV-Vis in combination with EPR... FT-ICR-MS confirms that the molecular formula is Co(phen)2(OH)2

nodes.name: In situ electrodeposition of Co-PH
nodes.procedure: The Co-PH films were electrodeposited from soluble Co(phen)2(OH)2 in 1.0 M NaOH. Typically, the Co-PH catalyst film was in situ deposited on FTO at a constant potential of 1.7 V_RHE in the Co(phen)2(OH)2 containing 1.0 M NaOH electrolyte at room temperature (298 K). Besides, the counter Pt electrode was separated by a Nafion membrane and was immersed in a 1.0 M NaOH electrolyte as well.
nodes.source_text: The Co-PH catalyst film was in situ deposited on FTO at a constant potential of 1.7 V_RHE in the Co(phen)2(OH)2 containing 1.0 M NaOH electrolyte...

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Co(OH)2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.233 g Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.07 g of NH4F, and 0.240 g of CO(NH2)2 were dissolved in 100 mL deionized water under stirring for 30 min. Then, the obtained solution was transferred to a 50 ml Teflon-lined autoclave with an FTO immersed in the solution as the growth substrate. The reaction was maintained at 120°C for 10 h.

nodes.name: CoOOH electrodeposition and activation
nodes.procedure: The FTO with an efficient exposure area (0.283 cm²) was used as a substrate. A constant current of 0.283 mA for 100 s and subsequent 2.83 mA for 60 s was applied on FTO in a 1.0 M CoSO4 aqueous solution. The as-deposited film was then activated at 1.4 V_RHE for 100 s in 1.0 M NaOH to trigger the phase transformation from Co(OH)2 to CoOOH. The final catalyst film was cleaned with deionized water for further experiments.

nodes.description: Mass activity and TOF of freshly electrodeposited Co-PH (10 min at 1.7 V_RHE)
nodes.source_text: The mass activity of electrodeposited Co-PH displays ~100 times (1.67 A mg⁻¹ at an overpotential of 350 mV) enhancement in comparison to that of pf-CoOOH. In addition, Co-PH was found to have a high TOF value of 0.35 s⁻¹ per total metal site under 350 mV overpotential, which is ~140 times higher than that of pf-CoOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Co K-edge XANES shifts 1.22 eV to higher energy for pc-CoOOH (vs pf-CoOOH) from OCP to 1.7 V_RHE, indicating higher Co valence ~+3.9. k^3-weighted EXAFS shows Co-O at 1.93 Å, Co-Co at 2.89 Å for both.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As is confirmed by a shift (1.22 eV) of XANES to higher absorption energy upon the potential switching from open circuit potential (OCP) to 1.7 V_RHE for pc-CoOOH than that of pf-CoOOH ... the k^3-weighted Fourier-transformed Co K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) reveals a Co-O distance of 1.93 Å and a Co-Co distance of 2.89 Å.
